Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring parents be notified when a juvenile is taken into custody.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to juvenile interrogation; adding a new section tochapter 13.40 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 13.40 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature finds that parents have a fundamental interestin knowing if their child has been taken into police custody forquestioning and where their child is being held. (2) When a law enforcement officer takes a juvenile into custody,a reasonable attempt must be made to notify a parent, guardian, orcustodian that the juvenile is in custody and where the juvenile isbeing held.

(1) By July 1, 2006, the administrativeoffice of the courts shall, within existing resources, convene andchair a work group to review statewide practices, protocols, andpolicies on the interrogation of juveniles in the custody of lawenforcement. p. 1 SB 6579 (2) In addition to the administrative office of the courts, thework group shall be comprised of the following members: (a) The attorney general or the attorney general's designee; (b) A member designated by the Washington prosecutors association; (c) A member of the Washington state patrol, designated by thechief of the state patrol; (d) A member designated by the Washington association of sheriffsand police chiefs; (e) A member of an organization that provides assistance to personswho are victims of juvenile crime, designated by the administrativeoffice of the courts; (f) A member designated by the Washington association of criminaldefense attorneys; (g) A member of an organization providing legal defense services tochildren, designated by the administrative office of the courts; (h) A member of an organization that primarily provides services tochildren and families involved with the criminal justice system,designated by the administrative office of the courts; and (i) An academic with a doctorate degree in child development,designated by the administrative office of the courts. (3) Members of the work group shall serve without compensation butmay be reimbursed for travel expenses as provided in RCW 43.03.050 and43.03.060. (4) The chair of the work group shall report to the appropriatecommittees of the legislature on the work of the work group not laterthan January 1, 2007.
